from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex signals are sums of simple sine waves.",
            "Think of an orchestra playing a single chord.",
            "Fourier reveals individual notes within that chord."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Intuition: The 'Orchestra' Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        melody = Circle(color=WHITE, radius=0.5)
        instruments = VGroup(*[Square(color="#FF00FF", side_length=0.4) for _ in range(3)])
        
        # Place elements
        self.place_at_grid(melody, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(instruments, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(Create(melody))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(instruments))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(
            melody.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            instruments.animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Foundation: Basis Functions", [
            "Fourier series defines signals by basis functions.",
            "Sine and cosine waves act as independent axes.",
            "They combine to reconstruct any complex wave."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw sine wave #FFFFFF with label f1
        sine_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x * PI), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FFFFFF")
        f1_label = Text("f1", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(sine_wave, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(f1_label, "B1")
        self.play(Create(sine_wave), Write(f1_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw higher frequency wave #FF00FF with label f2
        high_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x * 2 * PI), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FF00FF")
        f2_label = Text("f2", color="#FF00FF", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(high_wave, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(f2_label, "C2")
        self.play(Create(high_wave), Write(f2_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display summation formula #00FFFF for basis functions
        formula = MathTex(r"f(t) = \sum a_n \sin(nt) + b_n \cos(nt)", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "E4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating Coefficients: The 'Sieve' Method", [
            "Integration extracts the amplitude of each component.",
            "The integral acts as a precise frequency filter.",
            "It sieves out specific components from signals."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        # Signal: irregular wave
        signal = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x * 2) + 0.3 * np.cos(x * 5), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(signal, "B2", "C5")
        
        # Sieve: simple box or line acting as filter
        sieve = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=DOWN*1.5, color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(sieve, "B3")
        
        # Coefficient output
        coeff = Text("Amplitude: 0.5", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(coeff, "E3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(signal))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(sieve))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(sieve.animate.shift(RIGHT*2), FadeIn(coeff))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Adding terms creates sharper, more accurate waves.",
            "Convergence improves as we add more terms.",
            "Gibbs phenomenon causes overshoot at signal corners."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave Demo", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axes for visualization
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-PI, PI], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Target Square Wave
        square_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 if x > 0 else -1, color=WHITE)
        
        # Initial state: Show square wave outline
        self.add(square_wave)
        
        # Function to generate Fourier sum
        def fourier_sum(n_terms):
            def func(x):
                res = 0
                for i in range(n_terms):
                    n = 2 * i + 1
                    res += (4 / (np.pi * n)) * np.sin(n * x)
                return res
            return func

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Adding terms creates sharper, more accurate waves.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        f1 = axes.plot(fourier_sum(1), color="#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(f1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Convergence improves as we add more terms.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        f10 = axes.plot(fourier_sum(10), color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(Transform(f1, f10))
        
        # Error bar
        error_bar = Line(start=axes.c2p(2, 0), end=axes.c2p(2, 0.5), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(error_bar))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Gibbs phenomenon causes overshoot at signal corners.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Show overshoot zoom/highlight
        overshoot = Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 1.2))
        self.play(Create(overshoot))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "Fourier transforms time-domain to frequency-domain data.",
            "Spectrum analyzers visualize these frequency components.",
            "Compression algorithms use this to remove data."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Waveform
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(wave))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Spectrum analyzer with asset
        analyzer_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/analyzer.svg", color="#FF00FF")

        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.5, width=0.2, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.7) for _ in range(5)])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(bars, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Simple animation for bars to avoid heavy updaters if possible
        self.play(FadeIn(analyzer_icon), AnimationGroup(*[GrowFromEdge(b, DOWN) for b in bars], lag_ratio=0.1))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Compression illustration
        rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color="#00FFFF")
        text = Text("Data", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        comp = VGroup(rect, text)
        self.place_at_grid(comp, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(comp))
        self.play(comp.animate.scale(0.5))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Language of Waves

sections.title: The Core Intuition: The 'Orchestra' Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any complex, periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves. Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of periodic functions (sin/cos). Visual: A messy, jagged wave gradually morphs as we add smooth sine waves together.
sections.example: Imagine a musician playing a chord on a piano; the ear hears one 'complex' sound, but a Fourier Series reveals the individual pure notes (frequencies) that constitute that chord.

sections.title: The Mathematical Foundation: Basis Functions
sections.content: Define the Fourier Series formula. Explain the concept of 'orthogonality'—how sine and cosine waves function like independent axes in a space. Visual: A 3D graph showing how multiple simple waves (the building blocks) align to reconstruct a square wave.
sections.example: Think of this like mixing primary colors (Red, Blue, Yellow) to paint any specific hue in a palette.

sections.title: Calculating Coefficients: The 'Sieve' Method
sections.content: Explain how we extract the amplitude of each component using integration. The integral acts as a filter that picks out specific frequencies. Visual: An animation showing a 'sieve' passing over a signal, leaving only the strength of a specific frequency component.
sections.example: Using a radio tuner: You turn the dial to 'sieve out' one specific station (frequency) from the noisy background of all radio waves in the air.

sections.title: Visualizing Convergence: The Square Wave Demo
sections.content: Show the progression of adding terms: n=1, n=3, n=10. Discuss the 'Gibbs Phenomenon' (the little overshoot at corners). Visual: A growing stack of sine waves creating sharper and sharper corners of a square wave.
sections.example: A robotic cat's motion controller: Approximating a sudden jump (square wave) using smooth motor rotations to ensure the mechanical joints don't snap.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Summarize how Fourier Series transform time-domain data into frequency-domain data. Final visual: A spectrum analyzer showing real-time bars rising as an audio signal plays.
sections.example: How your smartphone compresses a high-quality song (MP3) by removing the 'inaudible' frequencies identified via the Fourier process.
